reason: The lift module needs a secure place on the frame, so fitting its padded mount is a useful start.
expectation: The mount should attach to the whale frame, ready to support the lift module.

effect: The padded mount has no available operation yet, so another part likely needs fitting first.
reaction: The required order was not obvious from the board.
reason: Inspecting the frame should reveal which parts can be fitted now.
expectation: The frame will show its currently compatible parts.

effect: The frame needed its paper skin first, and inspection fitted it automatically.
reaction: The required first step is clearer now.
reason: The hatch should provide access through the newly fitted skin.
expectation: The hatch will fit into the whale's skin, leaving access to its workings.

effect: The hatch is fitted and keeps the controller and counterweight accessible.
reaction: The access purpose is clear now.
reason: The padded mount should provide a secure place for the lift module inside the whale.
expectation: The mount will attach inside the whale, ready for the lift module.

alternatives.reason: The fins also need fitting, but the module mount seems more directly related to the goal.

effect: The module mount still cannot be fitted, so another step must come first.
reaction: The hidden ordering is becoming a little frustrating.
reason: The fins are the remaining obvious exterior part to fit before installing the module.
expectation: The fins will attach to the whale.

alternatives.reason: Inspecting would confirm the available fitting, but the fins are a plausible next step.

effect: The fins are fitted, completing the whale's silhouette without contributing lift.
reaction: The distinction between the fins and the lift tile is useful.
reason: With the exterior parts fitted, the padded mount may now be ready to support the lift module.
expectation: The mount will attach inside the whale, ready for the lift module.

alternatives.reason: Inspection could confirm the next available fitting if the mount is still premature.

effect: The padded mount is now fitted, so the whale is ready for its lift module.
reaction: It is satisfying to finally have a place for the module.
reason: The balanced lift module can now be installed on its mount.
expectation: The lift module will fit securely inside the whale.

effect: The balanced lift module is installed in the whale; the exterior stop-button extension remains to be fitted.
reaction: The main assembly is coming together.
reason: The exterior extension should keep the lift module's stop button accessible.
expectation: The stop-button extension will attach to the whale and allow power to be cut from outside.

effect: The outside button is linked to the stop switch, and the lift module's low battery and counterweight placement is explained. The chapter goal is complete.
reaction: The pushrod and low-set weight made the finished assembly more understandable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the outside stop button was most worthwhile: it made the safety control accessible and explained how the module sits inside the whale.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying the mount twice before it was available was repetitive, especially because the required order was not apparent.

surprise.text: The fins establish the whale's shape but provide no lift; that comes entirely from the invented tile.

arbitrary.text: The mount had to wait until after the fins, but the results did not explain why that fitting order was necessary.

continue.text: Yes. I would like to see how the assembled whale carries the fair, although I hope the next construction makes its required order clearer.
